questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of zài wàibianr?
What does kǔ mean when referring to life or experience?
What does néng chī kǔ mean?
Where must the adverb hùxiāng go?
Give the literary expression about being away from home.

answers.answer_text: Zài jiā qiān rì hǎo, chū wài yì shí nán — "At home one thousand days are good, but when one is on the outside even one moment is difficult."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I'm worried about my grandmother's health."
Write the Chinese for "We can learn from each other."
What do many Chinese think young people ought to be able to do?

answers.answer_text: Néng chī kǔ — to be able to take hardship.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "You don't need to worry."

articles.text:
10. A: Wǒ mǔqin zǒng dānxīn wǒ gēge My mother is always worried that my
       zài wàibianr chī kǔ.         older brother is having a rough time
                                     away from home.
    B: Tāmen jǐge xiǎo péngyou     His bunch of friends help each other
       hùxiāng bāng máng, bú huì    out. They don't have such a rough
       chī kǔde.                    time.

Notes on No. 10

dānxīn: "to be worried (that)"

Nǐ bú bì dānxīn, háizi dàle,     You don't need to worry. When the
tā zìjǐ huì dǒngde.              child grows up he'll understand.
Wǒ dānxīn wǒ nǎinaide shēntǐ.    I'm worried about my grandmother's
                                 health.
Tā dānxīn tā zuòbuhǎo nèijiàn    He's worried he won't be able to do it
shì.                             well.

zài wàibianr: Literally, "on the outside," a common way of saying "AWAY FROM HOME" or "away from one's hometown." The Chinese have an expression (in literary style):

Zài jiā qiān rì hǎo, chū wài yì shí nán
"At home one thousand days are good, but when one is on the outside even one moment is difficult."

chī kǔ: "to have a rough time, to suffer hardships." Kǔ, "bitter," when referring to life or an experience, means "hardship, suffering, pain."

Tā chīle bù shǎo kǔ cái cóng     He went through some rough times before
dàxué bìyè.                      he graduated from college.

Néng chī kǔ means "to be able to take hardships," "to have fortitude."

Zhōngguo hěn duō rénde kànfǎ shi In China many people think that young
niánqīng rén yīnggāi néng chī    people ought to be able to take
kǔ.                              hardship.

hùxiāng: "mutually, reciprocally, with each other." This is an ADVERB, so it must go AFTER the subject and BEFORE the verb.

Wǒmen kěyi hùxiāng xuéxí. Nǐ     We can learn from each other. You teach
jiāo wǒ Yīngwén, wǒ jiāo nǐ      me English and I'll teach you Chinese.
Zhōngwén.
